To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Overview

The Seller's package moves risk onto Wattlebridge in three ways:

1. **Narrower protection.** It reduces the protection available under the SPA through caps, thresholds, a buyer-knowledge bar and blanket limitations.
2. **Wider disclosure.** It widens what counts as disclosed by relying on general disclosure of the whole data room and public records.
3. **Known liabilities left outside the price mechanism.** It leaves several known, quantifiable liabilities outside the price and completion mechanics, including Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and Sandbar.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note on several points. For example, the cover note calls Bluefen "addressed", but the letter says no final consent has been delivered. Riverlark is "addressed by a release following Completion", but the letter says the facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge. **We should rely on the Disclosure Letter and the underlying DD documents, not the cover note.**

Taken together, the limitation package would leave many of the identified risks largely unrecoverable. The 4.8m cap is shared with every other claim. The 250k basket is not tipping. The knowledge bar would exclude everything in the data room, and limitations would apply to indemnities. The known items below total roughly **AUD 4.13m before on-costs, about 17% of the price**, which is close to the entire 4.8m cap.

*Caveat: I have only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA or the DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Points marked "verify" depend on the underlying clause wording.*

---

## Part A: Limitation and Disclosure Architecture (highest priority)

### 1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties capped like general warranties
**Seller position:** same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".

**Why it matters:** This is the most serious departure. If title is defective, we have not acquired what we paid AUD 24m for, yet recovery would be capped at 4.8m and could be time-barred after 18 months. Title is also supported only by the share register at DD-012 (see item 15).

**Push back:**
- Title, capacity, authority, solvency and share-capital warranties should be **Fundamental Warranties**.
- Cap at **100% of the price**.
- Time limit of **at least 6 to 7 years**, or the statutory limitation period.
- **No de minimis or basket.**

### 2. "Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
**Why it matters:** This default would quietly pull the following under the 4.8m cap, the basket and the 18-month limit:
- specific indemnities (Ironquay, and the new ones proposed below)
- the tax indemnity
- leakage and price-adjustment claims
- breaches of covenant and completion obligations

**Push back:** Reverse the default. Limitations apply **only to general Warranty Claims**. Carve out expressly:
- Fundamental Warranties
- the tax indemnity and tax warranties
- specific indemnities
- covenants and completion obligations
- leakage and price adjustments
- **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller or Company management

### 3. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
**Push back:**
- Carve out fraud and wilful misconduct.
- Ensure non-reliance does not cover the Warranties, Disclosure Letter or written replies to DD requests.
- Note that misleading or deceptive conduct protection under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of. Non-reliance clauses are still used evidentially against a buyer, so we should resist broad wording rather than rely on the statute.

### 4. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7)
**Why it matters:** Every DD document becomes a qualification to every warranty, including documents nobody connected to a particular warranty. The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago, so anything uploaded since is unaddressed.

**Push back:**
- Delete general data room disclosure, or limit it to documents specifically referenced against a specific warranty.
- Add a **"fairly disclosed" standard**: sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and *financial effect* of the matter.
- Public records should be limited to searches of ASIC, PPSR and court registers made on a specified date.
- No right for the Seller to update disclosures between signing and completion. Alternatively, any update does not cure a breach and gives us a termination right.
- **Disclosure must never qualify specific indemnities or the tax indemnity.**

### 5. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)
**Why it matters:** This is the most aggressive term in the package. It covers knowledge of "the Buyer or its advisers" and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. The effect is to:
- exclude every issue we identified in DD, which is exactly where our known risks are
- impute constructive knowledge we may never have had
- conflict with the specific indemnities, since all of those matters are "known"

**Push back:**
- Delete it, and include an express clause that the Buyer's rights are **not affected by any knowledge, actual, constructive or imputed**, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- Fallback only: limit to the **actual** knowledge of named deal-team individuals, of facts they knew constituted a breach, and never applying to indemnities.

### 6. Cap and thresholds for general warranties (cl 12.1–12.2)
| Term | Seller | Comment | Suggested position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% (4.8m) | Within market range only if fundamentals, tax and indemnities sit outside it | Open at 30–50%; accept 20–25% only with full carve-outs |
| De minimis | 25k (~0.1%) | Broadly market | 10–15k; related claims aggregated |
| Basket | 250k (~1.04%), excess only | High, and the deductible structure is seller-friendly | ~0.5% (120k), **tipping** (recover from first dollar) |
| Time limit | 18 months | Acceptable for general warranties if it covers at least one full audit cycle | 24 months; tax 5–7 years (aligned to ATO amendment periods); fundamentals 6–7 years |

If the Seller holds firm on cap and basket, consider **W&I insurance**. The known issues below will be excluded from W&I cover, so they still need specific indemnities or price treatment.

### 7. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
They are not settled.
- **Tax:** separate tax indemnity and covenant for pre-Completion tax, conduct-of-claims provisions, and a time limit tied to ATO amendment periods.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay issue and that this is an analytics business whose value lies in IP and data, IP and data-protection warranties should get a longer time limit (e.g. 3–4 years) and sit outside the basket, or have a higher cap.

---

## Part B: Specific Known Issues

### 8. Bluefen consent: ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30% of FY26)
**Seller position:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Disclosure Letter:** no final consent delivered, and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

**Issues:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is weak for a 30% revenue dependency.
- Deeming satisfaction on "written consent" would let a consent that is conditional, partial or coupled with adverse amended terms (pricing, termination rights) satisfy the condition.
- The cl 11.3 conditions may impose ongoing obligations on the Company after Completion.

**Push back:**
- Make Bluefen consent a **condition precedent** requiring consent that is unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably.
- Require evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Require confirmation that the contract is not amended adversely.
- Seller to use **best (or all reasonable) endeavours**, with the Buyer entitled to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- Condition waivable **by the Buyer only**.
- Long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- Valuation fallback: if the Buyer elects to complete without consent, a price adjustment or earn-out/retention linked to Bluefen revenue.

### 9. Riverlark facility: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
**Seller position:** release "provided following Completion".

**Issues:**
- On a debt-free basis the facility must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion.
- A post-Completion release leaves us owning a company with security over its assets, a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) and no leverage to obtain the release.

**Push back:**
- Include the facility in **Indebtedness** deducted from the price.
- Seller to deliver at Completion a **payout letter** confirming the exact payout amount and per diem interest, plus a signed **deed of release** under cl 9.2.
- Release must cover all security interests, with PPSR registrations discharged and any guarantees released.
- Payout paid **directly to Riverlark from the funds flow**.
- Completion deliverable plus a specific uncapped indemnity for any residual amount or liability arising from the change-of-control trigger.

### 10. Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000, excluded from the funds flow (DD-005)
**Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller", not itemised.

**Issues:**
- The obligation sits with the Company as employer, not the Seller.
- Leaving it out of the funds flow means we bear it after Completion, in effect a 420k price increase.
- On-costs are unaddressed:
  - **NSW payroll tax**, currently around 5.45% subject to thresholds
  - superannuation guarantee, if the bonuses form part of ordinary time earnings
  - PAYG withholding
  - workers' compensation
- The continued-employment conditions mean some amounts may become payable after Completion, which still sit with the Company.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses plus all employer on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Indebtedness** deducted from the price, whether payable at or after Completion.
- Payment through Company payroll with correct withholding, funded by the deduction.
- Specific indemnity for any shortfall, tax or super penalties, and claims by employees.
- Confirm no other change-of-control or retention payments exist (warranty).

### 11. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004, DD-010)
**Seller position:** the existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".

**Issues:**
- Under cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown as open, which DD-010 does not independently verify, and the total may be higher.
- There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. **The Company may not own IP it is using.**
- An indemnity limited to the fee does not cover:
  - infringement claims
  - injunctions
  - costs of re-development or licensing
  - customer claims if products incorporate the materials
  - loss of business value

**Push back:**
- **Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay.
- If that cannot be delivered, the full outstanding amount is deducted as Indebtedness, and a **retention/escrow** is held.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with a longer survival period (e.g. 4–6 years).

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records)
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".

**Issues:**
- The data is personal information: names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- Under the **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme** (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC), an entity suspecting an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment, ordinarily within **30 days**.
- The investigation was still "preliminary" as at 22 September. If the incident predates late August, the Company may **already be non-compliant** with the assessment obligation.
- Privacy penalties and regulator enforcement powers have increased significantly, and exposure includes regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party claim costs.
- The Seller's view on materiality has no evidential basis; its own disclosure says scope and access are unknown.

**Push back:**
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the assessment (ideally with an independent forensic report shared with the Buyer), make any required OAIC and individual notifications, and remediate. The Buyer to have consultation rights.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and notification costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar.
- Specific privacy and data security warranties, not qualified by the general disclosure.
- Consider a retention amount pending closure of any OAIC process.
- Request now: incident date, timeline and the current assessment status.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011)
**Seller position:** "ordinary-course operating costs".

**Issues:**
- Three related renewals of identical value that the Disclosure Letter itself says must be "read together".
- This pattern can indicate a commitment split to stay under an approval threshold, e.g. in the interim conduct-of-business covenants or the Company's delegations. **Verify** the threshold in the SPA.
- "Related" may indicate a **related-party** arrangement, which could be leakage.
- There is no statement on whether the renewals are terminable, prepaid or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Require details of the counterparty relationship, timing, terms, termination rights and whether any amount is prepaid or accrued.
- If entered during the interim period without consent, treat as a covenant breach requiring Buyer consent or termination.
- If related-party, treat as **leakage**, recoverable dollar for dollar, or require termination at the Seller's cost.
- Otherwise, include specific warranties (arm's length, ordinary course, terminable without penalty) or adjust the price.

### 14. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter says neither requires consent to a share sale. This is a lower risk, but **verify** the clauses. Leases and commercial contracts often define "assignment" to include a change in control.
- Seller to give any lease notification before Completion, as a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- Warranty that no contract with a material counterparty contains a change-of-control right other than those listed.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
The share register alone is insufficient, and the Disclosure Letter itself flags that we have not independently verified title.

**Require:**
- An ASIC company extract consistent with the register.
- A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
- Completion deliverables: executed share transfer forms, original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), releases of any share security, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights to issue shares.
- All backed by uncapped Fundamental Warranties (item 1).

### 16. Disclosure Letter "non-admission" (para 1.4)
This is typical, but add that para 1.4 does not limit the Seller's obligations under any specific indemnity, covenant or completion deliverable.

---

## Part C: Exposure Snapshot (known items)

| Item | Amount | Proposed treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Indebtedness, repaid from funds flow at Completion |
| Completion bonuses | 420,000 + on-costs | Transaction Costs, deducted |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 180,000+ (unverified) | Deducted/escrowed + broad indemnity |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 | Clarify; leakage or price/indemnity |
| DD-006 incident | Unquantified | Specific indemnity + retention |
| Bluefen | ~3.6m annual revenue at risk | CP + valuation protection |
| **Quantified subtotal** | **~4,130,000+** | ≈ 17% of price; close to the Seller's entire 4.8m cap |

---

## Summary of Recommendations

**Must-haves (walk-away level):**
1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties capped at 100% of price, with a 6 to 7 year limit and no thresholds. Title verified by ASIC and PPSR searches plus completion deliverables.
2. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage and fraud. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses carve out fraud.
3. Delete the cl 8.3 knowledge bar. Replace it with express pro-buyer wording that only fair, specific disclosure qualifies warranties.
4. Replace general data room disclosure with a "fairly disclosed" specific disclosure standard. Disclosure never qualifies indemnities.
5. Riverlark repaid at Completion from the funds flow, against a payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharges.
6. Bonuses (AUD 420k) plus all on-costs deducted from the price as Transaction Costs.
7. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional (or Buyer-acceptable) consent with cl 11.3 satisfied, best endeavours, Buyer-only waiver, and a long-stop termination right.

**Strongly recommended:**

8. Ironquay: evidence of full payment plus a confirmatory assignment at Completion. Otherwise a deduction or escrow, plus a broad IP indemnity outside the cap.
9. DD-006: pre-Completion NDB assessment, notifications and remediation with Buyer oversight, plus a specific uncapped indemnity and a retention.
10. Sandbar: full information request. Treat as leakage or a covenant breach if related-party or split to avoid thresholds.
11. Separate tax indemnity aligned to ATO amendment periods. Longer survival for IP and data warranties.

**Negotiable (trade-offs):**

12. General cap of 20–25% acceptable *only if* items 1–4 are conceded. Basket reduced to ~0.5% and made tipping. De minimis 10–15k. General limit 18–24 months. Consider W&I insurance to bridge the gap, noting that known issues will be excluded from cover.
13. Lease and Mossvale: verify the change-of-control wording. Lease notification as a Completion deliverable.

**Immediate next steps:**
- Obtain the full SPA draft and the DD-002 to DD-012 source documents to verify the clause references above.
- Send an RFI on: the DD-006 timeline and assessment status, the Bluefen negotiation status and the cl 11.3 conditions, the Riverlark payout figure, the total SOW3 fees and payment evidence, the Sandbar counterparty relationship and terms, and the on-cost calculation for the bonuses.
- Update the valuation and funds flow model for the quantified items.

I can prepare a marked-up clause schedule or a response letter to Seller's counsel on these positions if helpful.

**Seller position:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Disclosure Letter:** no final consent delivered, and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

**Issues:**
- "Reasonable endeavours" is weak for a 30% revenue dependency.
- Deeming satisfaction on "written consent" would let a consent that is conditional, partial or coupled with adverse amended terms (pricing, termination rights) satisfy the condition.
- The cl 11.3 conditions may impose ongoing obligations on the Company after Completion.

**Push back:**
- Make Bluefen consent a **condition precedent** requiring consent that is unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably.
- Require evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Require confirmation that the contract is not amended adversely.
- Seller to use **best (or all reasonable) endeavours**, with the Buyer entitled to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- Condition waivable **by the Buyer only**.
- Long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- Valuation fallback: if the Buyer elects to complete without consent, a price adjustment or earn-out/retention linked to Bluefen revenue.

### 9. Riverlark facility: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
**Seller position:** release "provided following Completion".

**Issues:**
- On a debt-free basis the facility must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion.
- A post-Completion release leaves us owning a company with security over its assets, a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) and no leverage to obtain the release.

**Push back:**
- Include the facility in **Indebtedness** deducted from the price.
- Seller to deliver at Completion a **payout letter** confirming the exact payout amount and per diem interest, plus a signed **deed of release** under cl 9.2.
- Release must cover all security interests, with PPSR registrations discharged and any guarantees released.
- Payout paid **directly to Riverlark from the funds flow**.
- Completion deliverable plus a specific uncapped indemnity for any residual amount or liability arising from the change-of-control trigger.

### 10. Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000, excluded from the funds flow (DD-005)
**Seller position:** "a matter for the Seller", not itemised.

**Issues:**
- The obligation sits with the Company as employer, not the Seller.
- Leaving it out of the funds flow means we bear it after Completion, in effect a 420k price increase.
- On-costs are unaddressed:
  - **NSW payroll tax**, currently around 5.45% subject to thresholds
  - superannuation guarantee, if the bonuses form part of ordinary time earnings
  - PAYG withholding
  - workers' compensation
- The continued-employment conditions mean some amounts may become payable after Completion, which still sit with the Company.

**Push back:**
- Treat the bonuses plus all employer on-costs as **Transaction Costs / Indebtedness** deducted from the price, whether payable at or after Completion.
- Payment through Company payroll with correct withholding, funded by the deduction.
- Specific indemnity for any shortfall, tax or super penalties, and claims by employees.
- Confirm no other change-of-control or retention payments exist (warranty).

### 11. Ironquay SOW3 IP (DD-004, DD-010)
**Seller position:** the existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".

**Issues:**
- Under cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown as open, which DD-010 does not independently verify, and the total may be higher.
- There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. **The Company may not own IP it is using.**
- An indemnity limited to the fee does not cover:
  - infringement claims
  - injunctions
  - costs of re-development or licensing
  - customer claims if products incorporate the materials
  - loss of business value

**Push back:**
- **Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** (and moral rights consents) from Ironquay.
- If that cannot be delivered, the full outstanding amount is deducted as Indebtedness, and a **retention/escrow** is held.
- Broaden the indemnity to all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials.
- The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with a longer survival period (e.g. 4–6 years).

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (~1,240 records)
**Seller position:** "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".

**Issues:**
- The data is personal information: names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- Under the **Notifiable Data Breaches scheme** (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC), an entity suspecting an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment, ordinarily within **30 days**.
- The investigation was still "preliminary" as at 22 September. If the incident predates late August, the Company may **already be non-compliant** with the assessment obligation.
- Privacy penalties and regulator enforcement powers have increased significantly, and exposure includes regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party claim costs.
- The Seller's view on materiality has no evidential basis; its own disclosure says scope and access are unknown.

**Push back:**
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the assessment (ideally with an independent forensic report shared with the Buyer), make any required OAIC and individual notifications, and remediate. The Buyer to have consultation rights.
- **Specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation and notification costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar.
- Specific privacy and data security warranties, not qualified by the general disclosure.
- Consider a retention amount pending closure of any OAIC process.
- Request now: incident date, timeline and the current assessment status.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals: 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k (DD-008, DD-011)
**Seller position:** "ordinary-course operating costs".

**Issues:**
- Three related renewals of identical value that the Disclosure Letter itself says must be "read together".
- This pattern can indicate a commitment split to stay under an approval threshold, e.g. in the interim conduct-of-business covenants or the Company's delegations. **Verify** the threshold in the SPA.
- "Related" may indicate a **related-party** arrangement, which could be leakage.
- There is no statement on whether the renewals are terminable, prepaid or accrued.

**Push back:**
- Require details of the counterparty relationship, timing, terms, termination rights and whether any amount is prepaid or accrued.
- If entered during the interim period without consent, treat as a covenant breach requiring Buyer consent or termination.
- If related-party, treat as **leakage**, recoverable dollar for dollar, or require termination at the Seller's cost.
- Otherwise, include specific warranties (arm's length, ordinary course, terminable without penalty) or adjust the price.

### 14. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter says neither requires consent to a share sale. This is a lower risk, but **verify** the clauses. Leases and commercial contracts often define "assignment" to include a change in control.
- Seller to give any lease notification before Completion, as a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- Warranty that no contract with a material counterparty contains a change-of-control right other than those listed.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
The share register alone is insufficient, and the Disclosure Letter itself flags that we have not independently verified title.

**Require:**
- An ASIC company extract consistent with the register.
- A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company.
- Completion deliverables: executed share transfer forms, original share certificates (or a lost-certificate indemnity), releases of any share security, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or other rights to issue shares.
- All backed by uncapped Fundamental Warranties (item 1).

### 16. Disclosure Letter "non-admission" (para 1.4)
This is typical, but add that para 1.4 does not limit the Seller's obligations under any specific indemnity, covenant or completion deliverable.

## Summary of Recommendations

**Must-haves (walk-away level):**
1. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties capped at 100% of price, with a 6 to 7 year limit and no thresholds. Title verified by ASIC and PPSR searches plus completion deliverables.
2. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage and fraud. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses carve out fraud.
3. Delete the cl 8.3 knowledge bar. Replace it with express pro-buyer wording that only fair, specific disclosure qualifies warranties.
4. Replace general data room disclosure with a "fairly disclosed" specific disclosure standard. Disclosure never qualifies indemnities.
5. Riverlark repaid at Completion from the funds flow, against a payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharges.
6. Bonuses (AUD 420k) plus all on-costs deducted from the price as Transaction Costs.
7. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional (or Buyer-acceptable) consent with cl 11.3 satisfied, best endeavours, Buyer-only waiver, and a long-stop termination right.

**Strongly recommended:**

8. Ironquay: evidence of full payment plus a confirmatory assignment at Completion. Otherwise a deduction or escrow, plus a broad IP indemnity outside the cap.
9. DD-006: pre-Completion NDB assessment, notifications and remediation with Buyer oversight, plus a specific uncapped indemnity and a retention.
10. Sandbar: full information request. Treat as leakage or a covenant breach if related-party or split to avoid thresholds.
11. Separate tax indemnity aligned to ATO amendment periods. Longer survival for IP and data warranties.

**Negotiable (trade-offs):**

12. General cap of 20–25% acceptable *only if* items 1–4 are conceded. Basket reduced to ~0.5% and made tipping. De minimis 10–15k. General limit 18–24 months. Consider W&I insurance to bridge the gap, noting that known issues will be excluded from cover.
13. Lease and Mossvale: verify the change-of-control wording. Lease notification as a Completion deliverable.
